import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
titanic_df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Check the null values
print(titanic_df.isnull().sum())

# Create a countplot of survival by sex
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.countplot(x='sex', hue='survived', data=titanic_df)
plt.title('Survival by Sex')
plt.xlabel('Sex')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Survived')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a boxplot of age by survived
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.boxplot(x='survived', y='age', data=titanic_df)
plt.title('Age Distribution by Survival')
plt.xlabel('Survived')
plt.ylabel('Age')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_age.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a bar chart of mean fare by class
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.barplot(x='pclass', y='fare', data=titanic_df)
plt.title('Mean Fare by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Mean Fare')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_fare.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot of age vs fare
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='age', y='fare', data=titanic_df)
plt.title('Age vs Fare')
plt.xlabel('Age')
plt.ylabel('Fare')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_age_fare.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
